People who don't believe in having possessions strike me as people who do not value the fruit of labor. A possession represents you own or someone else's labor of creation. When you make your own things or at least trade the monetary fruits of your labor for a thing made by someone else, you value the time, skill and effort put into that thing's creation. Should you obsess over possessions, probably not, but you can have the things you want and need and value what it took for them to exist. I value the things I make or buy because they represent a trade I made of my own resources so that someone else could afford to do the same. Living as a minimalist is fine and the right thing to do for some people, but living without any possessions yet still consuming someone's labor for transient things disrespects their efforts. John Lennon was wrong. He saw possessions as shackles to the free spirit and the fleeting pursuits of self-joy, yet his very fortune and lifestyle was driven by the selling of possessions created from his music. He, like many celebrities, confused obsession and possession and therefore devalued the work of others while shamelessly promoting his own work. I think we should celebrate those who make things by owning their works and cherishing them for the time we have them. It honors them and promotes the notion of work with a purpose.
